lessons.title: Static Linting Rule Configurations with ESLint
lessons.description: ESLint catches errors and enforces code style automatically — it's your code's quality guardrail.

sections.heading: What is ESLint?
paragraphs: ESLint analyzes your JavaScript code without running it. It catches common errors, enforces coding conventions and helps maintain consistent code across your team.
list: Catches errors before they reach production
Enforces consistent coding style across a team
Configurable rules — turn on/off as needed
Integrates with VS Code for real-time feedback

codeExamples.heading: ESLint catches common mistakes
codeExamples.code:
// ESLint flags these issues:

let x = 5       // Missing semicolon (if configured)
const y = 5
y = 10           // Error: Assignment to constant variable

function foo(a, a) {}  // Error: Duplicate parameter name

console.log(x)
console.log(y)   // Warning: 'y' is assigned but never used
explanation: ESLint catches real bugs like constant reassignment and duplicate parameters.
It enforces style rules like semicolons, quotes and spacing.
Warnings highlight potential issues; errors prevent code from running.
Rules are fully configurable via .eslintrc or eslint.config.js.

practice.task: Install ESLint in a project and create a config that enforces no-unused-vars and no-undef rules. Test with code that triggers both warnings.
hints: Add a variable that's never used and test the rule.

keyTakeaways: ESLint catches errors and enforces style without running your code.
Rules are configurable — customize for your project's needs.
Integrates with VS Code for real-time error feedback.
Use it in CI/CD pipelines to enforce quality across the team.
lessons.challenge: Configure ESLint with a custom rule set for a team project, including rules for complexity, naming and formatting.

lessons.title: Automated Code Formatting with Prettier
lessons.description: Prettier formats your code consistently — no more debates about style.

sections.heading: What is Prettier?
paragraphs: Prettier is an opinionated code formatter. It rewrites your code to follow a consistent style — regardless of how you originally wrote it.
list: Formats code on save in VS Code
Supports JavaScript, HTML, CSS, JSON, Markdown and more
Integrates with ESLint for comprehensive code quality

codeExamples.heading: Prettier before and after
explanation: Prettier adds consistent spacing, semicolons and line breaks.
It handles indentation, trailing commas and quote styles.
Run on save for automatic formatting.

practice.task: Install Prettier and configure it to format on save in VS Code. Test with intentionally messy code.
hints: Install the Prettier VS Code extension.
Write messy code and save — observe the formatting.

keyTakeaways: Prettier automatically formats code to a consistent style.
Configure it with .prettierrc and enable format-on-save.
It eliminates style debates — everyone's code looks the same.
Use with ESLint for comprehensive code quality.
lessons.challenge: Set up Prettier with custom rules for your project (single quotes, 2-space indent, trailing commas) and verify it formats correctly.

lessons.title: Pre-commit Hook Automation via Husky & lint-staged
lessons.description: Automatically lint and format code before every commit — catching issues before they enter the repo.

sections.heading: Pre-commit hooks
paragraphs: Pre-commit hooks run automatically before each git commit. They can lint, format and test your code, preventing bad code from being committed.
list: Husky — sets up git hooks in your project
lint-staged — runs linters only on staged files (faster)
Together they ensure code quality before every commit
Catches issues early — before they reach CI or code review

codeExamples.heading: Setting up Husky and lint-staged
explanation: Husky initializes git hooks in your project with npm run prepare.
lint-staged runs linters only on files that are being committed.

practice.task: Set up Husky and lint-staged so that running git commit automatically runs ESLint and Prettier on staged files.
hints: Test by committing a file with lint errors.

keyTakeaways: Husky sets up git hooks that run automatically before commits.
lint-staged runs linters only on staged files for speed.
Together they prevent bad code from entering the repository.
This is the industry standard for maintaining code quality.
lessons.challenge: Set up a complete pre-commit pipeline: ESLint + Prettier + a quick test run, all triggered by Husky and lint-staged.
